intent.goal: A published release carries everything needed to verify it offline, and the release workflow itself proves the published assets verify.
nonGoals: Signing or verifying the crates.io, npm or PyPI channels, which keep their own provenance
An opt-out that publishes an unsigned release

sectionHeadings: 201: A release ships its attestation bundles, requires signing, and verifies what it published
3.1 The bundle is a release asset
3.3 The release verifies what it published
record.summary: Spec 019 records each archive's build-provenance attestation only in GitHub's attestation store and leaves the bundle as "a later additive refinement". This spec is that refinement and two more. Each archive's Sigstore bundle (`<archive>.intoto.jsonl`) is attached to the GitHub Release next to the archive, so an archive verifies offline. Signing is required on every `v*` tag: a build that cannot obtain the OIDC token or whose attestation step yields no bundle fails before any publish job runs. A final job in `release.yml` downloads what the release actually published and verifies it: every checksum, every attestation against both its attached bundle and the store, and the presence of every archive's SBOM and bundle. A failed check fails the release workflow.
record.title: A release ships its attestation bundles, requires signing, and verifies what it published
